question.text: Anti-dilution protection in AIF investments protects investors from:

answer.text: Reduction in their economic interest due to subsequent rounds being issued at lower valuations (down rounds)

explanation.text: The Logic: Anti-dilution / ratchet protection cushions the AIF when the investee company raises a subsequent round at a lower valuation than the AIF's entry round. The workbook describes the mechanism as providing additional shares to offset the dilution caused by the cheaper share issuance. The Trap: The protection is specifically about down-round price dilution. It does not address currency risk, listed-market volatility, or changes in the AIF's own management — those are separate risk categories. Note: Anti-dilution typically operates by issuing additional shares to the AIF at par or at a low price so that its effective per-share entry cost is brought closer to the new, lower round price.
